gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $419.99 eufy E340 + Smart Display E10 bundle costs the same as buying the two separately ($169.99 + $249.99 = $419.98), so the 8-inch screen adds $249.99. SwitchBot's $149.99 kit already includes its 4.3-inch monitor, and an extra SwitchBot monitor costs $69.99. No result works out how many detections the E340 gets per charge either: EFTM logged 1,090 in 33 days, against the roughly 1,800 that eufy's own rating implies.
standout_why: I compared against the cited smarthomeperfected.com page plus worthrated.com and drunvalo.net. Smart Home Perfected gives no prices and no battery life for the E340 or the SwitchBot. It lists only the SwitchBot's 5000 mAh battery and notes its monitor needs a power cable. WorthRated gives no prices and doesn't cover these two products. Drunvalo has part of it: the E340 battery lasts 'typically 2 months' and the E10 ran 'about 6 hours unplugged' in the author's testing, with the E10 priced at $249. None of the three compares the bundle price with the parts, works out a per-screen cost, or turns a measured battery test into detections per charge against the maker's rating.
decides: This confirms SwitchBot as the value pick and recasts eufy as a premium choice. The eufy bundle saves nothing over buying the two separately, and its screen alone costs $249.99. SwitchBot's whole doorbell-and-monitor kit is $149.99. The eufy bundle also costs $20 more than the $399.98 ChatGPT showed. On battery, the E340's 180-day rating only holds at about 10 detections a day. At the 33 a day EFTM logged, it lasted 33 days. Busy front doors should plan to wire it in or recharge it monthly.
